title: footgun: scan(glob) with a parameter named `glob` implies standard glob semantics where `*` matches within a single path segment and does not cross `/`.
detail: The glob is compiled to an anchored, case-insensitive regex where `*` becomes `.*`, which crosses `/` boundaries. So scan("src/*.json") also matches deeply-nested keys like src/a/b.json, and matching is case-insensitive. Same behavior in the batch path (indexedDbBatch.ts scan, line 79).

title: footgun: Doc comment says "Compare two semantic version strings (e.g. \"1.0.0\" vs \"1.0.1\")", implying real semver comparison.
detail: It only parses dot-separated numeric components with `Number(p) || 0`. Pre-release/build suffixes are not handled: "1.0.0-beta" parses its third component as Number("0-beta")=NaN→0, so "1.0.0-beta" compares equal to "1.0.0"; any non-numeric component silently degrades to 0, and "1.2" vs "1.2.0" are treated as equal (not newer). Drives hydration overwrite decisions (bootstrapHydration.ts:43) and bootstrap manifest selection.

title: footgun: assertValidBootstrapSnapshot is named as if it validates that the data is a valid bootstrap snapshot (i.e. a map of file paths to cartridges).
detail: It only asserts the value is a non-null, non-array plain object that is JSON-serializable. It does not validate keys as paths or values as ModuleCartridge shape, so arbitrary object payloads pass and are later written verbatim into the store by importAll.

title: deletePaths and movePaths bypass dirty-file tracking, leaving stale/lost dirty state
detail: deleteFile clears dirtyFiles, but deletePaths (line 31) and movePaths (line 42) do not touch dirtyFiles. Deleting a dirty file via deletePaths leaves its path permanently in dirtyFiles (getDirtyFiles reports a file that no longer exists); moving a dirty file leaves the OLD path marked dirty and the NEW path unmarked, so a subsequent saveToDisk of the new path is not tracked and the phantom old path lingers. getDirtyFiles consumers see an inaccurate change set.

title: moveMany applies all writes before all deletes over a single key snapshot, so overlapping moves can delete a just-written value
detail: allKeys is captured once; writes (moved targets) are flushed first, then every matched source key is deleted. When a move target collides with another move's source (e.g. moving a/b→a while a/b/c also exists, or two moves whose target equals another's source), the delete phase removes a key that the write phase just populated, silently dropping data. The write/delete sets are computed independently with no collision guard.

title: importAll clears the entire store before writing, with no shape validation of entries
detail: importAll opens a readwrite tx, clears the store, then puts every top-level key of the (only structurally-validated) snapshot as a file value. A snapshot that passes assertValidBootstrapSnapshot but contains non-cartridge or non-path entries wipes existing data and repopulates the store with garbage; the pre-clear means a malformed-but-JSON-serializable import destroys the prior VFS contents irrecoverably.

title: silent failure: empty-catch
detail: Real: the try/catch around the disk fetch swallows every error (network failure, CORS, malformed JSON from response.json()) and returns null with no logging or pdd-ignore marker. Callers readFile/readText interpret null identically to "file absent", so a transient fetch/parse failure is indistinguishable from a missing file and can silently yield an empty read or trigger create_empty hydration, masking real I/O errors.
